exchanges.question: Construction starting strong, Deere growth significantly above industry up 5% forecast. Are you seeing healthy industry growth and gaining significant share?
exchanges.answer: Underproduction last year in earthmoving particularly front part of year; building alignment with retail demand driving natural lift this year. Industry guide up 5% in earthmoving; road building also strong. Picked up share over past 12 months, particularly last six months with pricing adjustments end of last year.

exchanges.question: Better sense of baseline margin in each business. Could you break down $272 million tariff refund between segments?
exchanges.answer: Tariff run rate unchanged at $1.2 billion full year despite IEEPA/Section 122/Section 232 changes. Tariff splits unchanged: ~45% Construction & Forestry, ~33% Small Ag & Turf, ~20% large ag. Full year impact ~3 points. Refund $272 million: ~50% C&F, ~30% SAT, ~20% large ag.

exchanges.question: Not taking pricing to offset tariffs—what mitigation strategies? What progress over 12 months and what more could come?
exchanges.answer: Price forecast 1.5%-2% for equipment operations, in line with inflation rates excluding tariffs of 1.5%-2%. Not surcharging customers on tariffs given dynamic/inconsistent rates. Focusing on reducing tariff exposure through cost actions: resourcing, reshoring, exemptions, USMCA compliance. Full confidence will counter tariff impacts through cost measures. Back half more favorable on comps from tariffs and material costs.

exchanges.question: How to frame downside risk on global ag cycle broadly bouncing on bottom given abnormal geopolitical environment? Any historical periods for farmer behavior reference?
exchanges.answer: Couple years into downturn; less replacement; fleet age elevated. North America high-horsepower tractors and combines at very elevated fleet age. Used inventory healthier, particularly late-model equipment down 45% from peak. Customers experiencing margin pressure heightened by fertilizer increases, particularly Brazil with currency headwinds. Baseline expectation still recovery in 2027 depending on factors including policy improvements, geopolitical, fundamentals.

exchanges.question: Order trends in large ag, specifically seasonal products and trends by regions standing out?
exchanges.answer: Manage seasonal products through Early Order Programs. EOPs closed for 2026; production plan set. Opening EOPs for next year: sprayers opened weeks ago, running through end of August; planters June-end September. Very early indications on trends. Everything seen thus far supports view that 2026 marks bottom of ag cycle.

exchanges.question: Precision Ag expectations: See & Spray acreage coverage this year, retrofit orders tracking, Precision Essentials renewal rates 2025 cohort, list price increases comments?
exchanges.answer: See & Spray: year one 1M acres, last year 5M acres globally; year-to-date customers spraying more acres than last year. 50-60% herbicide savings demonstrated two years; driving utilization. Introduced See & Spray Green on Green Brazil. Now covering wheat, barley, canola. EOP take rates for 2027 exceed this year. Precision Essentials orders trending well; getting 4,000-5,000 new customer orgs in Operations Center. Renewal rate ~70% overall; second-year cohort over 90%. Harvest automation utilization >60% Northern Hemisphere, >80% Brazil.

exchanges.question: Cadence for Q3 and Q4 on sales and margins? Any items by region or segment causing deviation from normal seasonality?
exchanges.answer: Back half higher than front half; Q4 slightly higher than Q3. Large Ag: Q4 stronger than Q3; more Waterloo tractor shipments to North America in back half than front, abnormal seasonality. Small Ag normal seasonality with step downs Q3 and Q4. Construction & Forestry fairly balanced, Q4 slightly stronger. Nothing abnormal called out.

exchanges.question: Pricing expectations look more conservative than peers. Is that reflection of higher discounting?
exchanges.answer: Pricing adjustment this quarter driven by Brazil; took price down quarter-over-quarter. All regions expected price positive in large ag. 1% price guide full year. North America a bit better; other two lower, averages to 1%. Similar across businesses. Second half price looks better than first half given incentive lapping. Used inventory progress and incentive management position well.

exchanges.question: IEEPA $270 million clawed back—incremental headwinds from other tariffs bring back to $1.2 or true benefit versus initial guide? How to square improving price-cost when cost inflation ahead vs easier comps?
exchanges.answer: $1.2 billion run rate unchanged; $272 million refund new in quarter; nets to ~$900 million this year. Material inflation seen over quarter; back half benefits from lapping tariffs from prior year and indirect inflation from tariffs. Pricing much more favorable back half. Back half sees better absorption in large ag factories from significantly higher production rates for U.S. large tractors.

exchanges.question: Dealer base sentiment and feedback in North America on large ag? Dealer expectations on spring EOP? How CapEx looking into 2027?
exchanges.answer: Baseline expectation some level of recovery next year driven by fleet age, inventory work. JDF wholesale (used equipment financing) down over 15% year-over-year, freeing balance sheet for new sales. Old crop supplies about third remaining; commodity price increases support that. Dealer feedback varied: those aggressive on used most optimistic, some adding used fleet in select cases; others more moderate depending on inventory management. Dealers positive see good setup.

exchanges.question: Continuing market share improvements in South America—is that within existing product portfolio or driven by new product introductions?
exchanges.answer: Over last 15 years, steady linear increase in tractors and combines share supported by multiple fronts: new products, new technologies, outstanding dealer channel, product localization. Record product introductions last year topped this year with more: new combines, sprayers, planters, technologies like See & Spray, Starlink connectivity. Harvest settings automation highest utilization globally in Brazil. Extremely bullish on region; see opportunity for more growth.
